bundlingNotes: This is a pure title-premium rate manual; Wyoming's residential closings are handled by title companies (not attorneys), and this manual confirms the WY market convention -- matching most other 'scarce' states surveyed -- of pricing title premium and settlement/escrow/closing services as two entirely separate, unfiled/unpublished matters. A 2025-08-25 rate-filing update was confirmed to exist via Virtual Underwriter bulletin WY2025002 (Wyoming DOI approved a new Stewart rate submission), and its effective date exactly matches independent agent Black Hills Title's own WY rate-sheet vintage below -- but the actual updated Stewart PDF could not be located at a working public URL this session, so the 2016 vintage remains the only verifiable Stewart WY document.

calculatorUrl: https://ratecalculator.fnf.com/?ID=FNF&state=WY (ASP.NET WebForms postback flow, form id 'aspnetForm', control prefix ctl00$BodyContent$UcRateCalc1)
scenario: $500,000 purchase price, $400,000 loan amount, Laramie County (Cheyenne) (the standard-scenario county), Property Purchase (with or without financing) transaction type, Residential property type, tool defaults for all other policy questions, Concurrent Owner's+Loan rate eligibility answered Yes (the tool's own default first option).
methodology: Driven via plain HTTP POST (Python requests.Session(), not WebFetch -- WebFetch's HTML-to-markdown conversion strips the raw hidden ASP.NET fields needed to replay the postback), following this project's existing FNF recipe documented in CALCULATORS.md: GET the county-selection page, POST the county (own __EVENTTARGET), POST btnGeneralNext=Next, POST TranType$ddl=PropertyPurchase, POST AmountPurchase$txt=500000 then AmountLoan1$txt=400000 (each with its own __EVENTTARGET), auto-answer the revealed Concurrent-rate-eligibility question Yes, then POST btnFinish=Finish for the final Rate Summary. One correction to the prior recipe write-up worth flagging: the page also renders a hidden 'ctl00$btnDummy' submit button used only for Enter-key submission -- a naive first-submit-button-found selector picks this dummy button instead of the real 'Next'/'Finish' button and silently fails to advance the flow; always filter submit-button candidates for the actual button's own name substring ('Next'/'Finish') rather than taking the first match. No personal-data fields exist anywhere in this flow.
